title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE EXCAVATION OF REMAINS OF SOLDIERS KILLED IN THE KOREAN WAR
title_original: 6ㆍ25 전사자유해의 발굴 등에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Excavation of Remains of Soldiers Killed in the Korean War and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Duties of Remains Excavation and Identification Unit)
(1) The Remains Excavation and Identification Unit under Article 5 of the Act on the Excavation of Remains of Soldiers Killed in the Korean War (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") (hereinafter referred to as the "Excavation Unit") shall perform the following duties:
1. Investigation of the whereabouts of, and excavation of, the remains of soldiers killed in the war;
2. Identification of the remains of soldiers killed in the war and confirmation of their bereaved families;
3. Collection, preservation, and management of materials concerning the excavation of the remains of soldiers killed in the war;
4. Publicity concerning the excavation of the remains of soldiers killed in the war;
5. Other matters directed by the Minister of National Defense concerning the investigation, excavation, and identification of the remains of soldiers killed in the war.
(2) The head of the Remains Excavation and Identification Unit (hereinafter referred to as the "Head") shall exercise overall control over the duties of the Excavation Unit under the direction of the Minister of National Defense.
(3) Necessary departments shall be established within the Excavation Unit, and matters concerning their organization and division of duties shall be determined by the Minister of National Defense.
(4) The authorized number of military personnel and civilian military employees assigned to the Excavation Unit shall be determined by the Minister of National Defense.

Article 3 (Composition and Operation of Remains Excavation and Identification Committee)
(1) A Remains Excavation and Identification Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") shall be established within the Excavation Unit to maintain objectivity and impartiality in duties concerning the investigation, excavation, identification, etc. of the remains of soldiers killed in the war and to provide academic advice.
(2) The Committee shall deliberate on the following:
1. Deleted. <July 13, 2015>
2. Matters concerning recognition and identification of the remains of soldiers killed in the war under Article 10 of the Act;
3. Matters concerning payment of rewards under Article 12 of the Act;
4. Matters concerning compensation for losses under Article 13 of the Act;
5. Other matters determined by the Head concerning the investigation, excavation, identification, etc. of the remains of soldiers killed in the war.
(3) The Committee shall consist of not more than 10 members, including one chairperson.
(4) The Head shall serve as chairperson, and members shall be commissioned or appointed by the Head from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience in relevant fields and officers and civilian military employees belonging to the Excavation Unit.
(5) The term of office of a member commissioned under paragraph (4) shall be three years, and the member may be reappointed for one consecutive term only. <Amended on June 2, 2025>
(6) The chairperson shall represent the Committee and exercise overall control over its affairs.
(7) Where the chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to unavoidable circumstances, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act on his or her behalf.
(8) A majority of the incumbent members shall constitute a quorum for a meeting of the Committee, and resolutions shall be adopted by the affirmative votes of a majority of the members present.
(9) The Committee shall have one executive secretary to handle its affairs, and the executive secretary shall be designated by the chairperson from among the staff of the Excavation Unit.
(10) Matters necessary for the operation of the Committee, other than those prescribed in this Decree, shall be determined by the chairperson following a resolution of the Committee.

Article 3-2 (Exclusion, Challenge, and Recusal of Members)
(1) A member of the Committee shall be excluded from deliberation and resolution by the Committee where any of the following applies:
1. Where the member or his or her spouse or former spouse is a party to the relevant agenda item (including an executive officer where the party is a corporation, organization, etc.; hereinafter the same shall apply in this subparagraph and subparagraphs 2 and 4), or is a joint holder of rights or joint obligor with a party to that agenda item;
2. Where the member is or was a relative of a party to the relevant agenda item;
3. Where the member has provided testimony, statements, advice, research, services (including subcontracted services), or expert appraisal concerning the relevant agenda item;
4. Where the member, or a corporation, organization, etc. to which the member belongs, is or was an agent of a party to the relevant agenda item;
5. Where a corporation, organization, etc. in which the member serves as an executive officer or employee, or served as such within the preceding three years, has provided advice, research, services (including subcontracted services), or expert appraisal concerning the relevant agenda item.
(2) A party to an agenda item may challenge a member before the Committee where a ground for exclusion under any subparagraph of paragraph (1) applies to that member or circumstances make it difficult to expect impartial deliberation and resolution, and the Committee shall decide by resolution whether to uphold the challenge. In such cases, the member subject to the challenge shall not participate in that resolution.
(3) Where a ground for exclusion under any subparagraph of paragraph (1) applies to a member, or the member determines that there are circumstances making it difficult to expect impartial deliberation on his or her part, the member shall recuse himself or herself from deliberation and resolution on the relevant agenda item.

Article 3-3 (Dismissal of Committee Members)
The Head may dismiss a member from his or her commission or appointment where any of the following applies:
1. Where the member becomes unable to perform his or her duties for an extended period due to physical or mental infirmity, etc.;
2. Where the member has committed misconduct related to his or her duties;
3. Where the member is deemed unsuitable as a member due to neglect of duty, impairment of dignity, or other grounds;
4. Where the member fails to recuse himself or herself despite falling under a ground for exclusion under any subparagraph of Article 3-2 (1) or determining that there are circumstances making it difficult to expect impartial deliberation on his or her part;
5. Where the member personally expresses that it is difficult to perform his or her duties.

Article 4 (Allowances)
Members and relevant experts, etc. attending a Committee meeting may be paid allowances, travel expenses, and other necessary expenses within budgetary limits; provided, this shall not apply where a public official attends in direct connection with duties under his or her jurisdiction.

Article 5 Deleted. <July 13, 2015>

Article 6 (Measures to Protect Remains of Soldiers Killed in the War)
The term "certain measures prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 8 (4) of the Act means the following:
1. Installation of the information sign specified in attached Table 2 at the site where remains are discovered;
2. Protective measures and periodic site inspections to prevent changes to the condition of the site where remains are discovered, including flooding, freezing, collapse, or washing away;
3. Notification to the landowner, etc. of the discovery of remains.

Article 7 (Contents of Plans for Investigation and Excavation of Remains of Soldiers Killed in the War)
(1) A plan for investigation and excavation of the remains of soldiers killed in the war under Article 9 (2) of the Act shall include the following:
1. Verification of records related to research on the military history of the Korean War;
2. A plan for inquiries in areas subject to investigation;
3. Areas and periods for excavation;
4. Matters concerning control of excavation sites and maintenance of records.
(2) Notification of a plan for investigation and excavation of the remains of soldiers killed in the war under Article 9 (2) of the Act shall be made using the notice of investigation and excavation of remains of soldiers killed in the war in attached Form 1, and shall be given by visiting the landowner, etc. or by mail no later than seven days before commencement of the investigation and excavation.
(3) The identification document indicating authority to investigate and excavate the remains of soldiers killed in the war under Article 9 (6) of the Act shall be the identification card for personnel in charge of investigation and excavation of remains of soldiers killed in the war in attached Form 2.
(4) Matters necessary for investigation and excavation of the remains of soldiers killed in the war, other than those prescribed in this Decree, shall be determined by the Minister of National Defense.

Article 8 (Criteria for Recognition as Remains of Soldiers Killed in the War)
The Minister of National Defense may recognize excavated remains as the remains of soldiers killed in the war pursuant to Article 10 (1) of the Act where any of the following applies:
1. Remains excavated in an area where information concerning the burial of the remains of soldiers killed in the war has been received (including reports, testimony, etc.; hereinafter the same shall apply) and where there is a high likelihood that such remains are buried;
2. Remains excavated in an area where the possibility of burial of the remains of soldiers killed in the war has been confirmed through military history research and investigation;
3. Remains found with personal effects recognized as belonging to a soldier killed in the war, or excavated together with military supplies, including firearms, recognized as having been used in the Korean War.

Article 9 (Criteria for Identification of Remains of Soldiers Killed in the War)
(1) Upon recognizing remains as those of soldiers killed in the war pursuant to Article 8, the Minister of National Defense shall identify the remains by the following methods: <Amended on Dec. 11, 2012>
1. Comparison of personal effects excavated with the remains;
2. Analysis of materials, including historical records related to the Korean War and military service records of soldiers killed in the war;
3. Comparison of testimony from war veterans, local residents, informants, etc.;
4. Forensic anthropological analysis;
5. Forensic medical analysis, including genetic testing and comparison and superimposition (Superimpose).
(2) Where identification of the remains of soldiers killed in the war is difficult by the methods under paragraph (1), a determination shall be made following deliberation by the Committee.

Article 10 (Preservation of Excavated Personal Effects)
Personal effects excavated with the remains of soldiers killed in the war pursuant to Article 10 (4) of the Act shall be kept in a personal effects repository designated by the Minister of National Defense; provided, explosives and ammunition among the personal effects shall be handed over to the commander of the military unit having jurisdiction over the area where the remains were excavated.

Article 10-2 (Procedures for Handling Remains of United Nations Forces)
The investigation, excavation, and handling of the remains of United Nations forces pursuant to Article 10-2 (1) of the Act shall follow these procedures:
1. Remains presumed to be those of United Nations forces shall be investigated and excavated using the same methods and procedures as for the remains of soldiers killed in the war, and their identities and nationalities shall be ascertained;
2. The nationality of the remains of United Nations forces shall be determined in consultation with the relevant country;
3. Remains of United Nations forces whose nationality has been determined shall be handled in accordance with the requests of the relevant country.

Article 11 (Retention and Maintenance of Genetic Test Results)
(1) Relevant materials, including genetic test results, under Article 11 (2) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on Dec. 11, 2012>
1. A genetic testing consent form in attached Form 3;
2. An index of genetic testing information;
3. Files or printouts of genetic test results.
(2) Materials under paragraph (1) shall be retained at a genetic testing institution or location designated by the Minister of National Defense until the remains of the soldier killed in the war are identified or the person who consented to genetic testing, including his or her legal representative, requests their destruction.

Article 12 (Criteria for Payment of Rewards)
Rewards under Article 12 of the Act shall be paid in accordance with the criteria for payment of rewards in attached Table 3. <Amended on Apr. 2, 2019>

Article 13 (Procedures for Compensation for Losses)
(1) A person wishing to claim compensation for losses pursuant to Article 13 of the Act shall submit to the Minister of National Defense a claim for compensation for losses in attached Form 4 stating the injured person's personal details, etc., together with documents proving the losses.
(2) Upon receiving a claim for compensation for losses under paragraph (1), the Minister of National Defense shall investigate the facts and, where the losses are not caused by grounds attributable to the relevant landowner, etc., shall pay compensation following deliberation by the Committee.
(3) Where it is decided to pay compensation, the claimant shall be notified of payment using the notice of payment of compensation in attached Form 5 within 10 days after the date of the decision, and compensation shall be paid within one month after the date of notification.
(4) A person wishing to object to a decision on compensation for losses shall submit to the Minister of National Defense an objection to the decision on payment of compensation in attached Form 6 stating the injured person's personal details, etc., together with documents substantiating the details of the amount of losses.
(5) In cases under paragraph (4), the matter shall undergo deliberation by the Committee again, and paragraph (3) shall apply where it is decided to pay compensation for losses.

Article 14 (Delegation of Authority)
Pursuant to Article 15 of the Act, the Minister of National Defense shall delegate authority concerning the following matters to the Head: <Amended on Dec. 11, 2012; Oct. 14, 2021>
1. Formulation and implementation of implementation plans for investigation and excavation, etc. of the remains of soldiers killed in the war under Article 6 (3) of the Act;
2. Deleted. <July 13, 2015>
3. Requests for protective measures for the remains of soldiers killed in the war under Article 8 (4) of the Act;
4. Investigation and excavation of the remains of soldiers killed in the war under Article 9 of the Act, including formulation, notification, and consultation, etc. concerning investigation and excavation plans;
5. Recognition and identification of the remains of soldiers killed in the war under Article 10 of the Act;
6. Genetic testing and retention of materials under Article 11 of the Act;
7. Payment of rewards under Article 12 of the Act;
8. Compensation for losses under Article 13 of the Act.

Article 15 Deleted. <July 13, 2015>

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 20832, June 20, 2008>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on June 22, 2008.

Article 2 (Repeal of Another Decree)
The Decree on the Ministry of National Defense Remains Excavation and Identification Unit shall be repealed.

Article 3 (Transitional Measures concerning Remains Excavation and Identification Unit)
The Ministry of National Defense Remains Excavation and Identification Unit established pursuant to the former Decree on the Ministry of National Defense Remains Excavation and Identification Unit as at the time this Decree enters into force shall be deemed the Remains Excavation and Identification Unit under this Decree.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 23807, May 23, 2012>
(Decree Partially Amending the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Building Lease Protection Act and Other Decrees for the Protection of Personal Information)

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Transitional Measures concerning Amendment of Forms)
Forms under the former provisions as at the time this Decree enters into force may be used together with forms under this Decree until August 31, 2012.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 24224, Dec. 11, 2012>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation; provided, the amended provisions of attached Table 3 shall enter into force on January 1, 2013.

Article 2 (Applicability concerning Payment of Rewards)
The amended provisions of attached Table 3 shall apply beginning with persons receiving rewards for contributing to the excavation of remains excavated on or after January 1, 2013.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 25840, Dec. 9, 2014>
(Decree Partially Amending the Enforcement Decree of the Building Act and Other Decrees for Regulatory Improvement, Including Establishment of Regulatory Review Deadlines)

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on January 1, 2015.

Articles 2 through 16 Omitted.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 26393, July 13, 2015>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 26774, Dec. 30, 2015>
(Decree Partially Amending the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Excavation of Remains of Soldiers Killed in the Korean War and Other Decrees to Minimize Collection of Resident Registration Numbers)

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation. <Proviso omitted.>

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 27083, Apr. 5, 2016>
(Decree Partially Amending the Enforcement Decree of the Special Act on Payment of Retirement Benefits to Military Personnel Who Retired on or before December 31, 1959 and Other Decrees for Comprehensive Amendment of Statutory Forms)

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 29672, Apr. 2, 2019>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
<Wholly Amended on Dec. 22, 2020>

Article 2 (Applicability concerning Payment of Rewards)
(1) The amended provisions of subparagraph 3 (a) and (b) of attached Table 3 shall apply beginning with cases where a person provides his or her own genetic sample on or after January 1, 2019.
(2) The amended provisions of subparagraph 3 (c) of attached Table 3 shall also apply where a person provided his or her own genetic sample before this Decree enters into force.
<This Article Added on Dec. 22, 2020>

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 31274, Dec. 22, 2020>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Applicability concerning Payment of Rewards)
The amended provisions of subparagraph 4 of attached Table 3 shall also apply to bereaved family members for whom the remains of a soldier killed in the war were identified as a result of their provision, before this Decree enters into force, of materials such as a certificate of family relations containing personal details of the soldier killed in the war, a certified copy of the soldier's removed family register, a notification of death in action, or personal effects.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 32041, Oct. 14, 2021>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on October 14, 2021.

Article 2 (Transitional Measures Following Change of Authority to Formulate Master Plans)
A master plan formulated by the Head pursuant to the former provisions before this Decree enters into force shall be deemed a master plan formulated by the Minister of National Defense pursuant to the amended provisions of subparagraph 1 of Article 14.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 35562, June 2, 2025>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Applicability concerning Consecutive Reappointment of Members)
The amended provisions of Article 3 (5) shall also apply to members commissioned before this Decree enters into force; provided, a member who has already been consecutively reappointed more than once as at the time this Decree enters into force shall retain his or her position until the expiration of the term of office, notwithstanding those amended provisions.
